name: io.github.1145-am/syracuse-mcp-server
title: Syracuse Company News
description: Company & industry news for AI agents: typed, dated, sourced events. Free key or x402 pay-per-call.

tools.name: industry_clusters_list
tools.description:
Industry clusters
Look up industry ids for the `industry_id` filter on `stories_organization_list` and `stories_industry_location_list`. Pass `search` with an industry in plain words (e.g. "biotech") to get the closest clusters, best match first, each with a `search_score` (lower is closer). Without `search` it pages through all ~6,000 clusters, so always search. Each result has `topic_id` (the value to pass as `industry_id`), `representative_doc` (example industry names), `representation` (key words) and links to broader (`parent_*`) and narrower (`child_*`) clusters. Usually you can pass the plain-words `industry` filter instead; use this to pin an exact cluster. 20 results per page (`page_size` up to 100). Free: no API key or payment needed.

page.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

page_size.description: Number of results to return per page.

search.description: Industry to search for, in plain words (e.g. "biotech", "ev charging"). Optional, but without it every cluster is listed.

tools.name: location_groups_list
tools.description:
Location groups
List every valid location for the `activity_location` and `org_location` filters on `stories_organization_list` and `stories_industry_location_list`. Returns all ~430 groups in one response (no paging), as a hierarchy: UN regions (e.g. "Asia", "Southern Asia"), then countries by ISO code (e.g. "IN", "FR"), then states or provinces for the US (via Census regions such as "Midwest"), AE, CA, CN and IN (e.g. "US-TX" is Texas, "CA-08" is Ontario). Each item has `id` (pass this, or `name` such as "texas", to the filters), `name`, `parent` and `children` (links to the groups above and below it). Filtering on a group includes everything beneath it. Free: no API key or payment needed.

tools.name: api_key_create
tools.description:
Get a free API key
Create a free account for an email address and get an API key for the paid stories tools. Returns `{email, token, detail}`: send `token` as the API key on later calls. It works at once for 30 queries/month, rising to 300/month after the user clicks the verification link that is emailed to them. If the email is already verified, returns 403 and emails the existing key instead. Only call this with the user's own email and their consent. Not needed if you pay per call with x402. Free: no API key or payment needed.

tools.name: stories_retrieve
tools.description:
Story by URI
Fetch one story in full by its `uri` (the `uri` field of any result from `stories_organization_list` or `stories_industry_location_list`, e.g. `https://1145.am/db/14993951/Ai_Cloud-Bytedance_Volcano_Engine`). Returns the detailed story: the same fields as a list result plus archive.org links and `similar_stories`. Activities add `actors` (every organization, person, product or place involved, grouped by role) and `activity_locations`; an IndustrySectorUpdate adds `industry_sector`, `metric`, `locations` and `analyst_organization`. Pass `output=simple` for just the list-result fields. Returns 404 if no story has that uri. Payment: send an API key, or pay $0.02 per call in USDC on Base via x402 (charged only when the call returns results).

output.description: Output format. Defaults to "full". Use "simple" for the list-result fields only.

uri.description: The story's `uri`, as returned in stories results.

tools.name: stories_industry_location_list
tools.description:
Stories by Industry/Location
News stories about an industry and/or a place, e.g. biotech deals in Texas. Use this when there is no specific company in mind; for news about a named company use `stories_organization_list`. Pass `industry` (plain words, e.g. "biotech") or `industry_id` (from `industry_clusters_list`), and/or `activity_location` (from `location_groups_list`): at least one is required. Returns `{count, next, previous, results, data_last_updated}`. Each result is one story, newest first, with `activity_class` (its type), `label`, `headline`, `document_extract`, `published_date`, `published_by`, `document_url` and `uri`. 20 results per page by default (`page_size` up to 100); follow `next` or pass `page` for more. Use `stories_retrieve` with a story's `uri` for its full detail (people, organizations and places involved, by role). Filter by story type with `type` and by recency with `days_ago` (7, 30 or 90 days; default 90). If the response is HTTP 202 the same query is already being computed: retry after the Retry-After seconds. Payment: send an API key, or pay $0.02 per call in USDC on Base via x402 (charged only when the call returns results).

activity_location.description: Location group name or id (e.g. "texas", "india", "MidWest", "FR", "us-ca") where the story happened. Not case sensitive. Accepts multiple values. They must each match an id or name from the location groups endpoint (`/api/v1/location-groups/`, MCP tool `location_groups_list`).

activity_location_id.description: Location group identifiers (e.g., "Southern Asia", "BT", "US-CA") where the story happened. Case-sensitive. Accepts multiple values. They must each match an id from the location groups endpoint (`/api/v1/location-groups/`, MCP tool `location_groups_list`).

days_ago.description:
How far back to look, in days: 7, 30 or 90. Counted back from the date the data was last updated (the `data_last_updated` field in the response), not from today. Defaults to 90.

* `7` - 7
* `30` - 30
* `90` - 90

include_provenance.description: Add a `source_audit` field to each story explaining why it matched (which source it came from, its match score, and the entity that carried it). Defaults to false.

industry.description: Industry name to filter by, in plain words (e.g. "biotech", "cybersecurity"). Matched by meaning, so no exact name is needed. Accepts multiple values.

industry_context.description: Optional context aspects to anchor the industry search in. Pass each aspect as a separate value. Can be a broader category name or detailed examples (e.g. "Movie Industry" when searching for "Distribution", or "BOPP Film" and "BOPET Film" when searching for "Film"). Applied to every value of `industry` in the same request.

industry_id.description: Industry ID (topic ID) to filter by. Accepts multiple values. They must each match a topic_id from the industry clusters endpoint (`/api/v1/industry-clusters/`, MCP tool `industry_clusters_list`).

output.description: Output format. Defaults to "simple" (SimpleStory schema). Use "full" for the detailed response.

page.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

page_size.description: Number of results to return per page.

type.description: Only return stories of these types. Accepts multiple values; omit for all types. Values: IndustrySectorUpdate (Analyst or market-report findings about an industry sector rather than one company); CorporateFinanceActivity (M&A, investments, stock purchases); PartnershipActivity (Partnership between 2 or more organizations. Often, companies describe their customers as their partners. This type of activity covers both genuine partnerships and customer/supplier relationships); RoleActivity (Key change in senior personnel, e.g. replacing CEO); LocationActivity (Opening or closing a new location (e.g. setting up in EMEA or shutting down a factory in a particular town)); ProductActivity (New product launches); AnalystRatingActivity (Updates from industry analysts); EquityActionsActivity (Stock repurchases, dividends etc); FinancialReportingActivity (Notice that an organization is going to announce its financials); FinancialsActivity (Information about company financials, e.g. revenue or EBITDA); IncidentActivity (Adverse incidents e.g. safety); LegalActivity (Lawsuits or activities that could lead to lawsuits, e.g. SEC investigations); MarketingActivity (e.g. launching a new advertising campaign); OperationsActivity (Company operations news, e.g. we are investing in a new product, or we have just completed an security audit); RecognitionActivity (e.g. we are delighted to announce that we won Agency of the Year); RegulatoryActivity (Legal or regulatory activity affecting this organization, e.g. permit for drilling, or regulatory filing); IndustryEventActivity (Conferences, trade shows, award ceremonies and similar events an organization hosts or takes part in).

tools.name: stories_organization_list
tools.description:
Stories by Organization
News stories about a named company, e.g. Microsoft's acquisitions or senior hires. `org_name` is required and is a partial match. If the name is ambiguous, narrow it by where the company is based (`org_location`) or what it does (`industry`); `activity_location` keeps only stories that happened in a place. For news about an industry or region rather than a company use `stories_industry_location_list`. Each story's `matched_organizations` shows which company matched. Returns `{count, next, previous, results, data_last_updated}`. Each result is one story, newest first, with `activity_class` (its type), `label`, `headline`, `document_extract`, `published_date`, `published_by`, `document_url` and `uri`. 20 results per page by default (`page_size` up to 100); follow `next` or pass `page` for more. Use `stories_retrieve` with a story's `uri` for its full detail (people, organizations and places involved, by role). Filter by story type with `type` and by recency with `days_ago` (7, 30 or 90 days; default 90). If the response is HTTP 202 the same query is already being computed: retry after the Retry-After seconds. Payment: send an API key, or pay $0.02 per call in USDC on Base via x402 (charged only when the call returns results).

activity_location.description: Location group name or id (e.g. "texas", "india", "MidWest", "FR", "us-ca") where the story happened. Not case sensitive. Accepts multiple values. They must each match an id or name from the location groups endpoint (`/api/v1/location-groups/`, MCP tool `location_groups_list`).

activity_location_id.description: Location group identifiers (e.g., "Southern Asia", "BT", "US-CA") where the story happened. Case-sensitive. Accepts multiple values. They must each match an id from the location groups endpoint (`/api/v1/location-groups/`, MCP tool `location_groups_list`).

days_ago.description:
How far back to look, in days: 7, 30 or 90. Counted back from the date the data was last updated (the `data_last_updated` field in the response), not from today. Defaults to 90.

* `7` - 7
* `30` - 30
* `90` - 90

industry.description: Industry name the company must work in. Narrows which companies match `org_name`. Accepts multiple values.

industry_context.description: Optional context aspects to anchor the industry search in. Pass each aspect as a separate value. Can be a broader category name or detailed examples (e.g. "Movie Industry" when searching for "Distribution", or "BOPP Film" and "BOPET Film" when searching for "Film"). Applied to every value of `industry` in the same request.

industry_id.description: Industry ID (topic ID) the company must belong to. Narrows which companies match `org_name`. They must each match a topic_id from the industry clusters endpoint (`/api/v1/industry-clusters/`, MCP tool `industry_clusters_list`).

org_location.description: Location group name or id where the company is *based*. Narrows which companies match `org_name`, so it may only be used together with `org_name`. Not case sensitive. Accepts multiple values. Valid values come from the location groups endpoint (MCP tool `location_groups_list`). For stories that happened in a place use `activity_location` instead.

org_location_id.description: Location group identifiers (e.g., "Southern Asia", "BT", "US-CA") where the company is *based*. Case-sensitive. May only be used together with `org_name`.

org_name.description: Company name to find stories about (e.g. "Microsoft"). Partial match, so it can match several companies; narrow with `org_location` or `industry`, and check `matched_organizations` on each story to see which company matched.

output.description: Output format. Defaults to "simple" (SimpleStory schema). Use "full" for the detailed response.

page.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

page_size.description: Number of results to return per page.
